chunks: Al-Saffar, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:
That Ali عليه السلام amputated the grave-robber’s hand. So it was said to him: “Do you amputate concerning the dead?” He said: “Indeed, we amputate for our dead just as we amputate for our living.”

key_terms.لِأَحْيَائِنَا: for our living persons; on behalf of our living
key_terms.لِأَمْوَاتِنَا: for our deceased persons; on behalf of our dead
key_terms.نَبَّاشَ: a grave-robber; one who digs up graves to steal

ai.seo_question: Does Islamic law apply the punishment for theft to robbing the graves of the dead?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Ali عليه السلام applied the hadd punishment to one who robbed graves. It shows that violation of the property and sanctity connected to the deceased is treated with the same legal seriousness as violation against the living. The narration reflects judicial enforcement and the preservation of rights after death.
